import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 672

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/672](https://www.erdosproblems.com/672)
-/

namespace Erdos672

/-- Erdős problem 672 conjectures that the below holds for any $k ≥ 4$ and $l > 1$. -/
def Erdos672With (k l : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (s : Finset ℕ), s.card = k → ∀ᵉ (n > 0) (d > 0), n.gcd d = 1 →
    Set.IsAPOfLengthWith s k n d → ∀ q, ∏ i ∈ s, i ≠ q ^ l

/--
Can the product of an arithmetic progression of positive integers $n, n + d, ..., n + (k - 1)d$
of length ≥ 4, with $(n, d) = 1$, be a perfect power?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_672 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k) (l > 1), k ≥ 4 → Erdos672With k l := by
  sorry

/-- According to https://www.erdosproblems.com/672, Euler proved this. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
lemma erdos_672.variants.euler :
    Erdos672With 4 2 := by
  sorry

/-- According to https://www.erdosproblems.com/672, Obláth proved this.

[Ob51] Oblath, Richard, Eine Bemerkung über Produkte aufeinander folgender Zahlen.
J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1951), 135-139. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
lemma erdos_672.variants.oblath :
    Erdos672With 5 2 ∧ Erdos672With 3 3 ∧ Erdos672With 3 4 ∧ Erdos672With 3 5 := by
  sorry

end Erdos672

findings.description: The answer slot has the opposite polarity from the source's question. The right-hand side asserts that every admissible progression avoids every perfect power, i.e. that no example exists. Thus `answer(True)` would mean “no” to the source's existence question, and `answer(False)` would mean “yes”. In the scratch file I proved that this right-hand side is equivalent to the negation of the source's existential statement. With the answer value held fixed, the two answer-bearing statements are not equivalent.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/672 asks: “Can the product of an arithmetic progression of positive integers n,n+d,...,n+(k-1)d of length k≥4 (with (n,d)=1) be a perfect power?” It then says “Erdős believed not.” The same wording appears in https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/672. The source still records the question as open.
findings.suggested_fix: Negate the entire current right-hand side: `answer(sorry) ↔ ¬ (∀ᵉ (k) (l > 1), k ≥ 4 → Erdos672With k l)`. Equivalently, use an existential statement giving k≥4, l>1, positive coprime n,d, and q with `∏ j ∈ Finset.range k, (n + j*d) = q^l`. The helper and solved variants need no change.

reformulations.difference: The predicate represents the progression by a finite set satisfying a cardinality condition and `Set.IsAPOfLengthWith`, rather than directly using an indexed product. It also allows every natural-number base q, including 0 and 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive d, the map j ↦ n+j*d is injective. The AP condition forces s to equal the image of `Finset.range k` under this map; that image has cardinality k, and its product is exactly ∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(n+j*d). I proved the helper equivalent to this indexed formulation for every k,l. In all cases used in the file, k≥2 and n,d>0 make the product greater than 1, so bases 0 and 1 introduce no additional perfect-power possibilities when l>1; this equivalence was also proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/672 — full problem statement, remarks, variants, and current status
R. Obláth, Über das Produkt fünf aufeinander folgender Zahlen in einer arithmetischen Reihe (1950), pp. 222–223; https://publi.math.unideb.hu/load_doi.php?pdoi=10_5486_PMD_1950_1_2_4_29
M. A. Bennett and S. Siksek, A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums, arXiv:1709.01022v1, introduction and relevant bibliography; https://arxiv.org/e-print/1709.01022v1
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md and the accompanying data/problems.yaml, entry 672 — independent status cross-check
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. The Euler and Obláth cases agree with the source, and their solved tags are current; the main problem remains open. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles and contains the encoding equivalence, boundary tests, finite searches, and the polarity/correction proofs. The equivalence proofs have no `sorryAx` dependency. The canonical Erdős pages were retrieved through their public origin after ordinary requests hit Cloudflare. The 1951 paper's full text was not retrievable, but its four cases are explicit on the cited webpage and corroborated by Obláth's 1950 introduction and theorem. No repository files were edited; the target's content hash matches the specified commit.

not_demonstrated.reason: The polarity reversal does not make the formalized nonexistence conjecture trivially provable or refutable. Proving that its right-hand side negates the source's existential question establishes the review finding, but does not prove or disprove the declaration itself. Resolving that declaration without relying on the imported `sorry` would still settle the open perfect-power question.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created; its absence was confirmed. The earlier logical equivalence proofs are not a proof or disproof of the exact declaration requested here.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported defect concerns answer polarity, not a degenerate hypothesis or incorrect computable definition. It therefore supplies no short, honest proof or disproof of the statement as formalized.

submission.summary: Negated the main theorem’s entire quantified right-hand side so that a positive answer means an admissible perfect-power product exists. All other declarations, docstrings, references, and attributes remain unchanged. The requested Lean compilation succeeds with only the expected `sorry` warnings.
